figma.description: CDS Web Radio (@coinbase/cds-web 9.29.0). One option of a radio group; RadioGroup and RadioCell are not part of this set.

notes.message: The states are Interactable's, on the control alone: Control renders the Interactable as the div around the input and the circle (Control.tsx L169-L180), and the label is its sibling (L238-L264), so hovering or pressing the label text draws no Hover or Active. Hover and Active dim the Interactable's children (Interactable.tsx L52-L54, L61-L63); the hidden input is one of them, the circle the other. Their background stays transparent: transparentWhileInactive (Control.tsx L170) paints the control transparent, and Interactable blends the hover and pressed colours from that transparent background (Interactable.tsx L207, L289-L310).

Disabled takes disabled, and readOnly draws the same: Control passes disabled || readOnly to the Interactable and the label Text (Control.tsx L177, L250), and only disabled reaches the input (L191). The Interactable is a div, so it is [aria-disabled='true'] (Interactable.tsx L244) that dims it to 0.5 (L66-L68), and transparentWhileInactiveCss keeps its background transparent (L103-L106).

Focus is on the hidden input. The control around it draws the ring: :has(:focus-visible) sets a 2px solid outline in bgPrimary, 1px outside its border box (Control.tsx L53-L59). The Contract draws it as a 2px outside stroke with no gap. To-preview forces :focus-visible on every element of the specimen, so its Focus card also shows the outlines no real focus draws: the Interactable's own, offset 2px (Interactable.tsx L80-L85), and the circle's (Radio.tsx L47-L52), a presentation div that never takes focus (L124).

The control is 22px: the 20px circle and the 1px border Interactable gives every element (borderWidth = 100, Interactable.tsx L209), which Control doesn't override (Radio.tsx L91 takes borderWidth for the circle, so none reaches Control). Its colour is transparent (transparentWhileInactiveCss, Interactable.tsx L100-L102), so stroke is none and the size is fixed, the circle centred in it.

CDS lays out the label row with alignItems flex-start and centres the control in a box one body line high (Control.tsx L243-L246), so the control sits on the first line of the label. The Contract centres the control on the label instead. For a one-line label, the default, both place it 1px below the top of the 24px line; a wrapped label keeps the control on its first line in CDS, centred in Figma.

The dot fades and scales in when checked (checkboxOpacityEnterConfig and checkboxScaleEnterConfig, motion/checkbox.ts L6-L7, applied at Radio.tsx L100-L104), and the circle's border colour changes over 0.2s (Radio.tsx L41). The Contract draws the end of both. The dot renders only when checked (L128-L133), so it is hidden unless Checked=True.

children is optional. Without it Control renders the control alone, with no label row (Control.tsx L236), so an unlabelled Radio is this component with its Label layer hidden. A label that is not a string renders in a Box rather than a Text (L247-L263); the Contract models the string label of the docs examples (_webExamples.mdx L11-L18).

These props are not axes: controlColor (bgPrimary by default, Radio.tsx L87) colours the checked circle and dot with any Theme colour (the docs use accentBoldGreen and accentBoldPurple, _webExamples.mdx L91 and L100); background, borderColor and borderWidth restyle the circle (Radio.tsx L89-L91); controlSize and dotSize resize it (L98, L131); elevation adds a shadow (Control.tsx L178). indeterminate, from ControlBaseProps (Control.tsx L72, L104), only turns the label fg (L137): a radio draws no indeterminate mark.

Radio is imported from @coinbase/cds-web/controls: controls/index.ts L9 re-exports RadioGroup, which re-exports Radio (RadioGroup.tsx L15). CDS's own Code Connect file (Radio.figma.ts) maps a checked variant, a label text and a show label boolean, and a state whose disabled sets disabled (L9-L24). The Contract follows it for Checked (False, True) and State, and has no show label boolean: hiding the Label layer is the unlabelled Radio (see properties.label). RadioGroup and RadioCell are their own families.
